targets.authors: Peters, E., Västfjäll, D., Slovic, P., Mertz, C. K., Mazzocco, K., & Dickert, S.
targets.title: Numeracy and decision making.
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted a Replication Registered Report of Peters et al. (2006) examining numeracy as a predictor of positive-negative framing effect (Study 1), frequency-percentage effect (Study 2), ratio effect (Study 3), and bets effect (Study 4).
targets.outcome_quote: Numeracy was associated with weaker framing effect (η2p = 0.01, 90% CI [0.00, 0.02]), weaker ratio bias (Cramer’s V = 0.17, 95% CI [0.10, 0.24]), and stronger bets effect (η2p = 0.02, 90% CI [0.01, 0.04]), yet we found no support for the frequency-percentage effect (η2p = 0.00, 90% CI [0.00, 0.01]).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The close replication supports three decision effects but not the frequency-percentage effect using the original dichotomous numeracy analysis. Continuous-variable extensions support all four; this does not remove the failed close comparison.

reasoning: The OSF project supplies the completed matching article, authored by Zhu and Feldman; the registered report is no longer prospective. All four targeted studies belong to one original paper. The downloaded print bundles the main article, references, and supplementary text.
